purpose: Teach: 演歌/林檎/車庫/国宝/大西洋/スリル/毛皮/ビーフ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが演歌を好まれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he loved enka music.
lines.style: Soft, reflective opening. A half-smile in the voice—nostalgic but not sad. Slow pace, letting the memory settle. Slight upward lilt on 'enka' like sharing a small, fond discovery.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、秋になると林檎を箱で買われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and in autumn your father would buy apples by the box, wouldn't he?
lines.style: Warm, slightly teasing. A knowing laugh underneath. She's gently redirecting, adding her own memory. Conversational pace, intimate — the tone of someone finishing each other's sentences after decades.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが車庫で日曜大工をされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he'd spend Sundays doing carpentry in the garage.
lines.style: Same reflective tone as the first line. Quieter this time—the memory is becoming more internal. Steady pace. A pause before 'garage,' like he's watching the scene unfold in his mind.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、国宝の仏像をご覧になって涙されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your father wept when he saw that National Treasure Buddha statue, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Tender, but with an edge of gentle correction. She's saying 'I remember this too—and differently.' Slight emphasis on 'wept.' Warm but not sentimental—matter-of-fact about his emotion.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが大西洋を船で渡る話を聞かせて下さったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he told me stories about crossing the Atlantic by ship.
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly—this memory carries wonder. Still reflective, but with an undertone of child-like amazement. Gentle pace, but with more forward motion than the previous lines. A glimmer of delight.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様とスリルあるお話を楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you and your grandson loved those thrilling tales together, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Affectionate, almost playful. She's caught him in a small vanity—he shares stories with the grandchild just as his father shared with him. Warm laugh in her voice. Slightly quicker pace, lighter touch.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お母様の毛皮のコートを着させていただいたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, I was allowed to wear your mother's fur coat.
lines.style: Voice softens into something almost tender—this memory is intimate, touches something vulnerable. Very slow pace. Quiet reverence for the trust it represented. Slight tremor of gratitude underneath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お祝いの日にビーフステーキをお作りになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you made beef steak on celebration days, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Closes the circle. Warm, loving, slightly breathless with affection. Slower pace than her other lines—this one lingers. A soft fadeout on 'dear,' like she's tucking him in with the memory.
